text:
Predicates:

FOL ::: x performs in school talent shows often

FOL ::: x attends and is very engaged with school events

FOL ::: x is an inactive and disinterested member of their community

FOL ::: x chaperones high school dances

FOL ::: x is a student who attends the school

FOL ::: x is a young child or teenager who wishes to further their academic careers and educational opportunities

Premises:

FOL ::: If people perform in school talent shows often, then they attend and are very engaged with school events.

FOL ::: People either perform in school talent shows often or are inactive and disinterested members of their community.

FOL ::: If people chaperone high school dances, then they are not students who attend the school.

FOL ::: All people who are inactive and disinterested members of their community chaperone high school dances.

FOL ::: All young children and teenagers who wish to further their academic careers and educational opportunities are students who attend the school.

FOL ::: Bonnie either both attends and is very engaged with school events and is a student who attends the school, or she neither attends and is very engaged with school events nor is a student who attends the school.

Conclusion:

FOL ::: If Bonnie is either both a young child or teenager who wishes to further her academic career and educational opportunities and chaperones high school dances or neither is a young child nor teenager who wishes to further her academic career and educational opportunities, then Bonnie is either a student who attends the school or is an inactive and disinterested member of the community.
